intended_object: The category of conflations (admissible short exact sequences) of a class E of kernel–cokernel pairs in a preadditive category C. Its objects are the conflations, and its morphisms are commutative ladders of three vertical maps between them. This is the category of short exact sequences of an exact category, as in Bühler §2 and §5. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The definition is the full subcategory of `ShortComplex C` on the short complexes that satisfy `E.Conflation`. Here `E.Conflation` is an `ObjectProperty (ShortComplex C)`, and the structure requires each conflation to be a kernel–cokernel pair and the class to be closed under isomorphism. A morphism of short complexes is a triple of maps that makes both squares commute, which is exactly a morphism of conflations as in the literature. Being a full subcategory matches the standard definition, since the category of conflations is a full subcategory of the arrow-triple category.

The generality is natural: it works for any preadditive category and any conflation class. That class need not even satisfy the exact-category axioms, which is at least as general as the literature, where C is additive.

Mathlib has no notion of exact categories or conflations, so there is no counterpart.
